 Order

This miscellaneous appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being crestfallen by the award dated 08.07.2008 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal'), District-Mandsaur in Claim Case No.51/2007 on account of inadequacy of compensation amount and seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. The date of accident and negligence are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard is not in question.
As per the findings of the Tribunal in the case of grievous injury of Smt.Sohanbai vs Virendra Singh & Ors.

on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43330175/
1 the claimant, the amount of compensation has been awarded by the Tribunal is Rs.4,850/- with 6%
per annum interest from the date of filing of claim application till its realization.
3. Counsel for the appellant/claimant contended that the Tribunal has erred in the matter of awarding the compensation on lower side.
He further submits that Tribunal has not appreciated the fact that claimant has received serious injuries.
He also submitted that Tribunal has not awarded the proper compensation under the head of treatment and other heads, hence, seeks enhancement in the compensation.
He further submitted that tribunal has also committed error in exonerating the insurance company totally.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company supported the award impugned and has contended that the Claims Tribunal awarded the compensation is just and proper and no need for further enhancement and prays for rejection of the appeal.
5. I have heard counsel for the parties and have perused the record of the case.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that insurance company has not adduced any evidence regarding willful breach of policy condition on the part of the owner and driver.
He further submitted that claimant was third party and insurance company cannot be desolved from its liability and every person other than ensurer and insured.
Hence, the ensurer is liable to pay the amount of compensation.
He also submits that tribunal has committed error in holding that driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective licence at the time of the accident.

7. In the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, AIR 2017 SC 3668,
Apex Court has held that holder of licence for light motor vehicle (LMV) can drive tractor attached to trolley and there is no need to obtain separate endorsement.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, AIR 2017 SC 3668
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Apex Court has also held that a person having LMV licence can drive the vehicle of which weight is below 7500 kg.
and there is no separate endorsement for driving commercial vehicle.
Hence, the tribunal has committed error in exonerating the insurance company from its liability totally.
In view of above, in the considered opinion of this Court, insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the claimant with owner and driver, jointly and severally.
However ,the insurance company is first to pay the compensation.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances and more particularly the age of injured and her earning and also looking to the injuries of the claimant, it shall be appropriate to enhance the amount by Rs.10,000/- which shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal in its award from the date of filing of the application.
9. Resultantly, this appeal is partly allowed to the extent indicated herein above.
The insurance company is liable to pay the enhanced amount of Rs.10,000/- to the claimants jointly and severally with owner and driver.
However, first liability is fastened upon the insurance company to pay the compensation amount.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the same rate from the date of filing of the claim application till its realization.
